title: kv cache: spillover memory manager and eviction heuristics v2
author: Claire Zhang
description: Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and frequent small spillover operations were causing elevated tail latency on long-context workloads and increasing GPU memory churn. This PR iterates on the spillover memory manager and eviction heuristics (v2): introduces a compacting spillover allocator, heuristics to prefer coalescing contiguous KV fragments, paging thresholds per-model/sequence-length bucket, and a background defragmentation task that is bounded by CPU and I/O budgets. Summary of changes: 1) spillover/allocator: add compacting allocator with a two-tier free list (size-class + contiguous-run) and a fast-path for coalescing adjacent free ranges; 2) eviction heuristics: add age+size scoring with weight tapering based on model sequence-length histogram to reduce eviction of hot long-context keys; 3) paging: introduce adaptive paging-from-GPU thresholds that consider per-device available memory and recent allocation churn; 4) defragmentation: background defrag job that runs opportunistically and respects a per-node budget flag (kv.defrag_cpu_pct) and storage_throttle (kv.defrag_io_ops); 5) scheduling integration: inform request router of spillover pressure to prefer shorter-context replicas when under memory pressure; 6) metrics and observability: add spillover.fragmentation_ratio, spillover.coalesce_rate, kv.eviction_score_distribution, kv.defrag_cycles and a dashboard patch; 7) config: expose new runtime flags and defaults for dedicated/private deployments. Testing and validation: microbenchmarks across a variety of sequence-length distributions, end-to-end load tests on dedicated pools, and A/B canary rollout. Observed results (see perf_results): reduced fragmentation_ratio by ~3x on synthetic workloads and tail latency (p99) improvement of 18-25% on long-context Llama2-13B traces. Rollout plan: staged canary (10% traffic) for 48 hours, monitor spillover metrics and latency; then 50% for 24 hours; full rollout if no regressions. Rollback path: disable kv.spillover_compaction and revert allocator via a single config toggle. Backwards compatibility: config defaults maintain prior behavior; no breaking API changes. Related: references ENG-1732 (KV spillover followups) and ENG-1801 (continuous batching improvements).

discussion:
Evan: Can we avoid doing compaction during high QPS? Suggest adding backpressure signal.
Claire: Added kv.defrag_cpu_pct and defrag_io_ops to throttle; defrag worker checks recent_qps and will pause when > threshold.
Marta: How does this interact with continuous batching? Could defrag increase latency spikes?
Claire: We limit defrag CPU to a small budget and run it on background threads pinned to lower scheduling priority; also added a canary that measures batching latency under defrag load. Benchmarks showed negligible impact on median latency.
Samir: Need telemetry on eviction churn per model; recommend exposing per-model histograms.
Claire: Added kv.eviction_score_distribution and per-model labels on key metrics.
Evan: CI flake on allocator_test on first run.
Claire: Fixed race in free-list initialization and re-ran CI. All checks passed.
Approvals: Evan approved after addressing CPU budget; Marta approved after reviewing benchmarks; Samir gave final LGTM after per-model telemetry added.
release_notes: Improved KV cache spillover memory management and eviction heuristics (v2): compacting allocator, coalescing heuristics, adaptive paging thresholds, background defragmentation with CPU/IO budget controls, routing-aware pressure signals, and new observability metrics. Expected to reduce fragmentation and improve tail latency on long-context workloads.
